correctness.rationale: At the interior equilibrium, environmental stationarity gives x*=1/(1+θ) and the logit equation gives the stated n_β. Once β exceeds β_int this is between 0 and 1 because D−(r−θh)=t+θv>0. The Jacobian trace is pM(β−β_h), the off-diagonal entries have opposite signs, and at the stipulated interior Hopf point their negative product is ω²=εβ_hDp n_h(1−n_h)>0. The eigenvalue crossing speed is pM/2>0. With u=x−x* and w=(β_hpD/((1+θ)ω))(n−n_h), the unchanged time variable gives linear part (−ωw,ωu). Using z=(u−ωw+Aωuw)/p with A=a(1+θ)/D, the quadratic and cubic terms of the logit expansion are obtained from σ′=p, σ″=pq and σ‴=p(q²−2p), q=(θ−1)/(1+θ). In polar coordinates the mean cubic term is the mean of R₃−R₂Θ₁/ω; the quadratic radial mean is zero, and its iterated contribution to the full angular return vanishes as the integral of a derivative of the squared primitive. The environmental terms proportional to uw and uw² cancel in the mean. This gives 16pℓ=(Q−2)−(Q+2)ω², Q=Aq. The assumptions force Q<2 by 2D−a(θ−1)=(1+θ)(r+t+v−h)>0. Thus the signs and threshold follow, and the positive crossing puts attracting cycles on the β>β_h side for ℓ<0 and repelling cycles on the β<β_h side for ℓ>0. For the stated example a rational log(5) interval yields β_h>β_int, 0<n_h<1 and 0.0921526508<κ<0.0921526594, which suffices for opposite signs at ε=1 and 100. No cycle type is claimed at ℓ=0.
